question: Which relationship does the extends keyword model between a subclass and its superclass?
explanation: extends expresses an is-a relationship: a subclass is a specialized kind of its superclass. A has-a relationship is modeled with composition, where one class holds a reference to another.

question: Which description best defines composition in Java?
options: A subclass reuses the fields of a superclass through extends
A class is declared abstract so that it cannot be instantiated
A class holds a reference to another object in a field and delegates work to it
A class implements an interface to gain default methods
explanation: Composition builds a class from other objects held in fields, and the outer class forwards (delegates) calls to them. Inheritance reuses code through extends instead.

question: How many direct superclasses can a Java class have?
explanation: Java supports single class inheritance: a class has at most one direct superclass. Multiple behavior types are obtained through interfaces, not multiple superclasses.

question: A class declares no extends clause. What is its direct superclass?
options: Object, but only if the class is public
explanation: Every class without an explicit extends clause implicitly extends java.lang.Object, regardless of its access modifier. This is why every object has methods such as equals, hashCode and toString.

question: Which guideline best summarizes when to prefer composition over inheritance?
options: When the relationship is not a true is-a relationship, or when the collaborator should be replaceable at runtime
Only when the superclass is declared final
Only when you want to reduce the number of classes
Because composition makes method calls execute faster
explanation: Prefer composition when the classes do not share a genuine is-a contract or when behavior needs to be swapped at runtime. The choice is about design and flexibility, not performance.

question: What does the fragile base class problem refer to?
options: A subclass cannot be compiled without the superclass source code
A subclass being unable to call super methods
Changes to a superclass's internal implementation can break subclasses that depend on it
explanation: Subclasses often depend on how the superclass works internally, so a seemingly safe change in the superclass can silently break them. Composition reduces this coupling.

question: A developer needs a Stack class that exposes only push, pop and peek. Which design is best?
options: class Stack extends ArrayList<Integer>, exposing every list method
class Stack extends Object and copies all of ArrayList's code into itself
class Stack with a private ArrayList<Integer> field and public push, pop and peek methods that delegate to it
class Stack extends ArrayList<Integer> and overrides add to throw an exception
explanation: Composition hides the internal list, so callers can only use the intended operations. Extending ArrayList leaks its whole API and weakens the stack contract.

question: A subclass in a different package must access a superclass member through inheritance. Which is the least permissive modifier on that member that allows this?

explanation: If a subclass cannot honor the inherited contract, it is not a true specialization, which breaks the is-a relationship. Adding fields, calling super() and overriding toString are ordinary uses of inheritance.

options: A class may extend one class and implement several interfaces
A class may extend several classes but implement only one interface

question: Which statement best summarizes when inheritance is appropriate?
options: Whenever two classes happen to share a few methods
When the subclass is a true specialization of the superclass and honors its full contract
Whenever code reuse is desired, regardless of the relationship
Only when the superclass is declared final
explanation: Inheritance fits a genuine is-a relationship where a subclass can substitute for its superclass. Sharing code alone is better done with composition, and a final class cannot be extended at all.

question: What is dynamic method dispatch in Java?
options: Choosing the method to call at compile time from the declared type of the reference
Loading a class into the JVM only when it is first used
Selecting which overriding method runs based on the actual runtime class of the object
Invoking a method by name through reflection
explanation: With dynamic dispatch, the JVM decides at runtime which version of an overridden instance method to execute, using the actual class of the object rather than the declared type of the reference.

question: Which condition must an instance method in a subclass meet in order to override a superclass instance method?

It must have the same name and return type but may take any parameters
It must have the same name but a different number of parameters
It must use the same parameter names but may have any method name
explanation: Overriding requires the same name and the same parameter types (the same signature). A different parameter list creates an overload, which is a separate method.

The compiler reports only a warning and continues

question: Class A is in package one and declares a package-private method void m(). Class B is in package two, extends A, and declares void m() with the same signature. What is the relationship between the two methods?

question: Why might a designer declare a method final in a template-method design?

question: What is an abstract class in Java?

A class that contains only static methods

A class that cannot be extended
